glosses: The extent to which a subspace is curved within a metric space.

examples.text: A turtle drawing an ellipse would have to turn more per distance traveled to get around its “pointy” sides than to get around its flatter top and bottom. This notion of how “pointy something is,” expressed as the ratio of angle turned to distance traveled, is the intrinsic quantity that mathematicians call curvature.

glosses: The extent to which a Riemannian manifold is intrinsically curved.
To cause (something) to change its shape into a curve, by physical force, chemical action, or any other means.

glosses: To change direction.

examples.text: The road bends to the right.

glosses: To be inclined; to direct itself.

examples.text: to whom our vows and wishes bend

glosses: To stoop.

examples.text: He bent down to pick up the pieces.

glosses: To bow in prayer, or in token of submission.

examples.text: Each to his great Father bends.

glosses: To force to submit.

examples.text: They bent me to their will.

glosses: To submit.

examples.text: I am bending to my desire to eat junk food.

glosses: To apply to a task or purpose.

examples.text: He bent the company's resources to gaining market share.

glosses: To apply oneself to a task or purpose.

examples.text: He bent to the goal of gaining market share.

glosses: To adapt or interpret to for a purpose or beneficiary.

examples.text: Palladius did not lie, although he might have bent the facts a bit and even passed over in silence whatever might not have benefited his client's cause.

glosses: To tie, as in securing a line to a cleat; to shackle a chain to an anchor; make fast.

examples.text: Bend the sail to the yard.

glosses: To smoothly change the pitch of a note.

examples.text: You should bend the G slightly sharp in the next measure.

glosses: To swing the body when rowing.

glosses: Any of the various knots which join the ends of two lines.

examples.text: A simpler version of the common bend with its ends in the same direction is used to join binder twine in a hay baling machine.

glosses: A severe condition caused by excessively quick decompression, causing bubbles of nitrogen to form in the blood; decompression sickness.

examples.text: A diver who stays deep for too long must ascend very slowly in order to prevent the bends.

glosses: One of the honourable ordinaries formed by two diagonal lines drawn from the dexter chief to the sinister base; it generally occupies a fifth part of the shield if uncharged, but if charged one third.

examples.text: Perhaps the most celebrated coat of arms is that of Scrope, which is Azure a bend Or. This is the coat over which, from 1385 to 1390, Sir Robert le Grosvenor and Sir Richard le Scrope invoked the High Court of Chivalry to decide which of them had the right to bear these arms. Chaucer gave evidence before the court. In the end the arms were awarded to Scrope, and Grosvenor was ordered to difference with a bordure Argent. This he disdained to do, and being highly dissatisfied with the verdict he appealed to Richard II who altered the decision of the court by refusing to allow the bend to Grosvenor at all! Grosvenor then adopted a garb, or sheaf of corn.

glosses: Turn; purpose; inclination; ends.
